study: Somers et al. 2010 — Enhanced Reading Opportunities (ERO): RAAL & Xtreme Reading supplemental literacy (NCEE 2010-4021, MDRC)
eval_evidence: Independent NCEE/IES evaluation conducted by MDRC (Somers et al.); program developers are distinct from the evaluation team (collaboration is acknowledged but evaluation is contractor-run, NCEE 2010-4021).
developer_evidence: 'the programs' developers provided three types of training and technical assistance to the ERO teacher from each school' — initial training, booster sessions, and coaching delivered by the program developers themselves.
cascade_evidence: Program developers trained and coached the ERO teachers directly (onsite coaching visits to schools); district program coordinators only observed — no train-the-trainer hop to reach teachers.
counterfactual_evidence: Within-school student-level random assignment to ERO vs non-ERO; non-ERO students received the regular (business-as-usual) ninth-grade program with no supplemental literacy course.
coaching_evidence: Developers 'provided onsite support to the ERO teachers through instructional coaching visits to the schools both years' — recurring in-class coaching cycles across the year.
student_dose_evidence: ERO is a year-long supplemental ELECTIVE literacy COURSE in addition to regular English — students received ~11 hours/month of extra instruction (the non-ERO group did not), a substantial added student-facing instructional dose.
maturity_evidence: Each student receives a single year-long supplemental course; the reported headline pools two successive implementation cohorts (cohort-1 ES 0.09, cohort-2 0.08), i.e. measurement spans first and second implementation years but the program itself is one academic year per student.
